doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1959 Monterey Jazz Festival commissions
summary: Jimmy Lyons commissioned El Camino Real and Sketch for Trombone and Orchestra.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: We’d like to move on to the 1959 Monterey Jazz Festival and to two of your large works, El Camino Real and Sketch for Trombone and Orchestra that were presented as a part of the festival program that year.

I had heard about the Monterey Jazz Festival. Jimmy Lyons who was the entrepreneur and producer invited me to perform on that Monterey Jazz Festival and to write works for orchestra – well, jazz band, shall we say. I wrote those two works. One was El Camino Real which translated, I understand, means the king’s highway.
Right. The king's highway. And the other [was] Sketches for Trombone and . . .
Yes, Sketch for Trombone and Orchestra.

Yes, Sketch for Trombone and Orchestra, yeah. It didn’t enjoy repeat performances as El Camino Real did. For one thing, I never performed it any more, and I don’t know why. El Camino Real has remained a part of my big band library. When I ever have occasion to do a big band scenario, I usually include El Camino Real in that situation. All I remember is that Monterey is a beautiful jazz festival. It's near Big Sur. It's in a beautiful part of California. It's all outdoors, and people enjoy it for its scenic beauty as well as the music and the jazz ambiance.
And those were commissioned works from the Festival?
Yes, from the Festival, right. They were indeed.
